newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mostly firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mostly firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly firmer on Wednesday, helped by overnight gains in the currency, with activity light and many investors focusing on the June 2 federal election, analysts said.

"Activity is very subdued. There'd been a little bit of buying overseas in the longer dated bills when the currency looked like it topped out," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc. "Other than that it's been very very quiet."
Canada's three-month cash T-bill firmed to yield 3.02 percent from 3.03 percent at Tuesday's close.
Canada's dollar opened slightly stronger at C$1.3834 (US$0.7228) in moderate trading on Wednesday after some good interest overnight to buy the unit in the Far East.
Traders said polls showing a smaller-than-expected lead for Canada's governing Liberals ahead of the June 2 general election were injecting added volatility into the currency.

"The attention has turned to the elections to some degree. There's been increasing talk of the political situation in Canada, polls and what they mean for the government to come Monday in terms of majority versus minority," said Posiewko.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.43 percent from 3.45 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.95 percent from 3.98 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 2.95 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
